selectionReason: RC66 ended at the missing object-level identity and selection ledger. A July 2026 official MAST reprocessing created a new public layer that can test archive recoverability immediately without waiting for a second epoch or unpublished analysis files.
newVerifiedFacts: The MAST DOI inventory contains 115 JWST observation rows: 40 from GO-2875, 39 from GO-1995, and 36 from GO-1685.
The inventory contains 87 NIRCam image rows and 28 NIRISS image rows; 76 are associated with Adam Riess and 39 with Wendy Freedman.
NGC 3447 has six public observation rows in one visit, spanning only 0.0614 day, with NIRCam and NIRISS coverage in F090W and F150W plus NIRCam F277W and F356W.
The six observation rows expose 1,428 public products, including six level-3 CAT products generated by JWST pipeline version 2.0.1.
The official NIRCam F090W and F150W catalogs were generated on 2026-07-18 and contain 6,636 and 11,327 sources respectively.
The catalogs contain generic segmentation labels, sky positions, aperture and isophotal photometry, morphology, and nearest-neighbour information.
They contain none of the author stable ID, period, phase, correction, fit-inclusion, exclusion-reason, or covariance fields needed to execute 154-to-144-to-142 lineage.
No catalog label equals the author ID among coordinate matches within 0.3 arcsec in either band.
An even-ID development split selects the same rigid translation, +0.02 arcsec in RA*cos(dec) and -0.08 arcsec in declination, independently in both bands.
On the untouched 79 odd IDs, 25 F090W and 37 F150W positions recover a source within 0.3 arcsec; 15 recover a source in both bands.
Dual-band recovery at 0.3 arcsec is 14 of 30 tidal, 1 of 35 spiral, and 0 of 14 other validation objects; the tidal-versus-spiral Fisher odds ratio is 29.75 with two-sided p=4.095e-5.
Thirty-six five-arcsec shifted controls average 4.667 dual-band matches versus 15 at the frozen coordinates.

The F150W first-pass aperture magnitude minus published phase-corrected magnitude has RMS 0.312 mag across 18 validation matches at 0.1 arcsec, so it is not a substitute for the custom PSF measurement.
No second public NGC 3447 JWST epoch was found in the pinned target inventory; all six rows share one visit root.

hypothesisAdjudication.claim: The DOI itself closes the published Cepheid analysis ledger.
hypothesisAdjudication.reason: It closes observation and product identity, not author-ID, correction, selection, or covariance ancestry.

hypothesisAdjudication.claim: MAST CAT labels are the paper's stable Cepheid IDs.
hypothesisAdjudication.reason: They are generic segmentation labels and no coordinate match carries an equal author ID.

hypothesisAdjudication.claim: The first-pass catalog can reproduce the published F150W photometry.
hypothesisAdjudication.reason: The matched residual RMS is 0.312 mag and the products use segmentation/aperture measurements rather than the custom PSF pipeline.

hypothesisAdjudication.claim: The catalog contains a real coordinate-associated signal beyond local chance matches.
hypothesisAdjudication.reason: Frozen-position dual-band matches are 15, compared with 4.667+-1.867 in five-arcsec shifted controls.

hypothesisAdjudication.claim: The component recovery difference proves a causal crowding bias.
hypothesisAdjudication.reason: Component, source density, dust, morphology, background, and segmentation change together; forced photometry and matched injections are required.

hypothesisAdjudication.claim: A public second epoch can now adjudicate phase error.
hypothesisAdjudication.reason: The six public rows span one visit and 0.0614 day.

failedOrRejectedAttempts: Treating a DOI as a semantic analysis package failed because DOI holdings enumerate observations, not the paper's transformation ledger.
Joining author IDs directly to catalog labels failed in both bands.
Using nearest first-pass aperture magnitudes as Cepheid PSF magnitudes failed the residual diagnostic and violates the documented product purpose.
Interpreting the tidal-versus-spiral recovery contrast as crowding was rejected because the design does not isolate background from population and segmentation differences.
Searching the pinned target observations for a second epoch found only one visit.
Coordinate matching cannot recover the twelve identities missing between 154 corrections and 142 published rows.

workPackages.name: Target-first forced ledger
workPackages.output: Every published coordinate retains an explicit detected, unmatched, masked, and forced-flux state.
workPackages.pass: No target is dropped by catalog inclusion.

workPackages.name: Matched injection surface
workPackages.output: Band-by-band inclusion and residual surfaces over magnitude, colour, background, detector, and component support.
workPackages.pass: Independent pipelines agree within 0.02 probability and 0.01 mag where support overlaps.

workPackages.name: Selection-sensitive component contrast
workPackages.output: Complete-case, forced, and injection-weighted contrasts with full shared covariance.
workPackages.pass: All admissible changes remain below 0.01 mag in both reductions.

uncertaintyBudget: Astrometric transform: frozen on even IDs and varied only through preregistered sensitivity branches.
Chance alignment and deblending: measured with shifted controls and injection recovery.
Finite injections: simultaneous intervals by magnitude and background stratum.
PSF and calibration mismatch: independent reductions, exposure-specific residuals, and shared-ancestor covariance.
Population transport: no extrapolation outside component overlap; report partial-identification bounds instead.
Phase and unpublished selection: remain separate unidentified terms rather than being absorbed into catalog recovery.
unverifiedClaims: The component recovery contrast is caused by crowding.
Forced photometry will reproduce the paper's custom-PSF fluxes.
Injection weighting will move the published component contrast by less than 0.01 mag.
The proposed combination is absent from all prior literature.
The current archive contains every exposure or analysis file used by the authors.
